items.title: P&G Buys Supplements Maker Thorne For $3.8bn As Wellness Push Intensifies
items.summary: Procter & Gamble is acquiring supplements maker Thorne for $3.8 billion in cash from LVMH-backed private equity firm L Catterton.

items.title: Procter & Gamble acquires dietary supplement manufacturer
items.summary: Procter & Gamble, the American multinational primarily active in personal care and household products, is paying billions to acquire Thorne, a manufacturer of dietary supplements.

items.title: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners’ H1 Revenue Tops €10.7bn
items.summary: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP) reported total revenue of €10.7 billion for its first half of 2026.

items.title: Scandi Standard Acquires Ireland's Glenhaven Foods For €127m
items.summary: Swedish poultry producer Scandi Standard has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Ireland-based Glenhaven Foods for €127 million.

items.title: Mud Jeans files for bankruptcy, hopes for a fresh start
items.summary: The Dutch circular denim brand Mud Jeans has succumbed to an excessive debt burden and has filed for bankruptcy. CEO Dion Vijgeboom hopes, however, that this is not the end of the story.

items.title: Kraft Heinz Raises Forecasts As New CEO's Turnaround Push Drives Sales Beat
items.summary: Kraft Heinz raised its annual outlook after quarterly sales beat estimates, as price increases offset weaker volumes across key markets.

items.title: Former Carrefour CEO Daniel Bernard has died
items.summary: Daniel Bernard, who served as CEO of Carrefour from 1998 to 2005, passed away on the night of August 4–5. He expanded the retailer’s international operations, oversaw the merger with Promodès, and acquired GB, the Belgian market leader at the time.

items.title: Esselunga Posts H1 2026 Sales Of €4.8bn
items.summary: The board of directors of Esselunga has approved the results for its first half of 2026, which saw total sales of €4.8 billion.

items.title: Heineken sells more beer and has already cut 3,000 jobs
items.summary: Somewhat contrary to expectations, Heineken sold more beer in the first half of this year, though not in Europe. The cost-cutting program, which will result in the loss of 6,000 jobs, is halfway through.

items.title: Bottler Coca-Cola HBC Lifts Profit Forecast As Demand Stays Strong
items.summary: Switzerland-based bottler Coca-Cola HBC narrowed its annual organic operating profit growth towards the higher side of its forecast range.

items.title: Tesco Ireland And Northern Ireland To Get New CEO
items.summary: Andrew Yaxley returns to the role of chief executive of Tesco Ireland and Northern Ireland, a role he held for three years previously.

items.title: E-commerce and Europe keep Ahold Delhaize on track
items.summary: While Ahold Delhaize’s margins are under pressure in the U.S., performance improved in Europe, particularly for Delhaize and Albert Heijn in Belgium. The retailer, which is reporting strong online sales, is maintaining its forecasts for the full fiscal year.

items.title: ABP Food Group invests in UK red-meats supplier Dovecote Park
items.summary: Ireland-based meat giant ABP Food Group has acquired a shareholding in UK beef-to-venison supplier Dovecote Park. The post ABP Food Group invests in UK red-meats supplier Dovecote Park appeared first on Just Food .

items.title: Shein worth only half as much at IPO
items.summary: Shein plans to go public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange this month and is aiming for a valuation of 30 to 40 billion U.S. dollars. That is much less than the fashion giant was once worth, as new import tariffs are eroding its profitability.

items.title: Africa, Asia boost Heineken H1 amid Americas struggles
items.summary: CFO Harold van den Broek said Heineken was “seeing the benefit of our global footprint” but conceded the brewer was “not happy” about the Americas.

items.title: Organic distributor Marma acquires eight brands from Distribio
items.summary: Consolidation in the organic sector continues: Starting August 1, Marma of Tienen will take over the distribution of eight organic food brands from Distribio. Both companies hope this will allow them to focus more on their core businesses.

items.title: Internal row at Castel rumbles on as family members file complaints
items.summary: The CEO of global drinks group Castel is facing two complaints from the daughter and nephew of the group’s founder Pierre Castel.

items.title: Columbia Sportswear calls off the search for the edge of the earth
items.summary: Columbia Sportswear’s CEO Tim Boyle has officially called off the search for the edge of the earth. This is the last instalment in its ‘Expedition Impossible’ campaign which called on the public to find the edge of the Earth in return for the keys to the firm. Columbia…

items.title: The biggest food M&A deals of 2026 so far
items.summary: Companies focused on clean-label ingredients and high-protein made up the bulk of acquisition activity as big brands strategically capitalize on new trends.

items.title: Penny Opens All-Wood Sustainable Store In Czechia
items.summary: Penny Česká Republika has opened a store built entirely from wood in Česká Lípa as part of its long-term strategy.

items.title: Italian Retail Sector Consolidates As Store Closures Rise – Confcommercio
items.summary: Italy’s retail sector is undergoing a structural shift toward larger, more corporate business models, according to Confcommercio.

items.title: Pinterest takes festival trends offline with UK corner shop pop-ups
items.summary: Pinterest has unveiled plans to open three festival-themed corner shop pop-ups across the UK in partnership with e.l.f. Cosmetics. The social media platform will launch the temporary stores in Brighton, East London and near Notting Hill Carnival, positioning each site on routes…

items.title: UK on brink of decades-low cereal crop – research
items.summary: The UK faces its worst cereal and oilseed harvests in decades as heatwaves and droughts cut yields, a non-profit has warned. The post UK on brink of decades-low cereal crop – research appeared first on Just Food .

items.title: Private Label Growth Outpaces Brands In Europe, IGD Study Finds
items.summary: Private label outperformed brands in Europe with sales growth of 4.1% in value in 2025 compared with 2.7% growth for manufacturer brands.

items.title: B&M to close two stores as part of huge estate overhaul
items.summary: B&M is set to close two stores this month as part of a wider overhaul of its UK estate, including relocations, expansions and investment in its existing shops. The company will permanently shut its Hall Street store in Carmarthen on 15 August before opening a larger branch at…

items.title: Ahold Delhaize's Second Quarter Core Profit Beats Expectations
items.summary: Ahold Delhaize has reported second-quarter core profit above market expectations, citing strong cost management and market-share gains.

items.title: Australian Vintage to distribute RTD brand Fellr
items.summary: Wine company Australian Vintage has struck a distribution partnership with Australian ready-to-drink brand Fellr.

items.title: Specsavers launches club guestlist with help from Groove Armada
items.summary: Specsavers has unveiled a club guestlist series for the over 50’s. Consumers can get on the guestlist by taking part in the company’s free online hearing screener. The ‘TestList’ was devised by PR agency Golin Ketchun, in partnership with Specsavers in-house creative team, media…

items.title: Kering turns to secondhand to lure back customers
items.summary: Kering is exploring ways to sell pre-owned items from Gucci, Balenciaga, and Saint Laurent directly. The luxury group hopes to win back consumers who have turned away due to steep price increases, without compromising on exclusivity.

items.title: De Bijenkorf logistics partner hit by a cyberattack
items.summary: A cyberattack on one of De Bijenkorf’s logistics partners is causing delays in orders, returns, and refunds. The department store is investigating whether the attackers were also able to access customers’ personal data.

items.title: US sports-drinks brand Barcode sold to PE firm Axum
items.summary: Barcode, the US drinks brand backed by NBA star Victor Wembanyana, is selling a “controlling” stake to private-equity firm Axum Capital Partners.

items.title: Broeklin, the successor to Uplace, lays the groundwork for its 2028 opening
items.summary: Development of Broeklin is getting underway. Earthwork has begun on the former Uplace site in Machelen. Construction is scheduled to begin later this year, with an opening planned for 2028.

items.summary: The Advertising Standards Authority has banned an advert from clothing brand Jaded London for “glamourising” smoking. The email, which appeared on 27 May 2026, was flagged by a complainant who challenged whether the campaign was irresponsible because it showed smoking to be…

items.title: SKIMS to launch in India with two flagship stores
items.summary: Kim Kardashian-founded fashion retailer SKIMS is set to debut in India with the launch of two new stores.

items.title: Next Century Spirits buys brands from Grain & Barrel
items.summary: US-based Next Century Spirits has acquired “certain brand assets" from local peer Grain & Barrel Spirits, including Chicken Cock whiskey.

items.title: Casella Family Brands adds RTDs and non-alc brands to distribution roster
items.summary: Casella has gained the distribution rights in Australia for the non-alcoholic drinks brand Heaps Normal and the spirits RTD line Four Loko.

items.title: BellRing Brands poised for price increases
items.summary: BellRing Brands plans to raise prices again on protein powders and shakes to recover inflationary costs.

items.title: Big Food fills up on DTC sales
items.summary: While sales directly from brands' digital platforms are unlikely to ever top brick-and-mortar, they allow food manufacturers to connect with consumers and test new products.

items.title: Jameson teams with NFL as global sponsor amid spirits market struggles
items.summary: The Pernod Ricard brand will have exclusive marketing rights as the official spirits sponsor of the league, which is continuing its international push.

items.title: Michael Kors’ disappointing performance weighs on Capri Holdings’ results
items.summary: Capri Holdings saw a decline in revenue in the first quarter of its fiscal year, primarily due to Michael Kors's underperformance, despite strong results from Jimmy Choo.

items.summary: Albena Georgieva discusses her return home to lead BILLA Bulgaria, following several successful years as COO of BILLA Slovakia.
